schema_note: Milestone 10C post-implementation held-out set -- written AFTER Strategy C was selected and implemented, specifically so it was NOT available to influence that selection (unlike evaluation/m10c/heading_controls.json, the 78-entry corpus used for Phase 2/3's design comparison). Fresh phrasing throughout, deliberately not literal duplicates of the main corpus's entries, to test generalization rather than memorized cases. Evaluation data only, exercised directly against the real, shipped `segmentation.py` via tests/test_m10c_heading_classification.py -- never imported by src/gitscore.

controls.rationale: Fresh REQUIRED-family phrasing, not in the main corpus (which has 'Required Skills'/'Required Qualifications' but not 'Required Experience').
Colon-terminated variant of an already-recognized phrase, different casing from the main corpus's bare 'Minimum Requirements' entry.
Fresh PREFERRED-family phrasing distinct from the main corpus's 'Preferred Skills'/'Preferred Qualifications'.

A natural real-world idiom variant of 'What You'll Do' -- flagged ambiguous from authoring, BEFORE this held-out set was run against the shipped classifier: the RESPONSIBILITY root is anchored to the exact phrase 'what you'll/will do' and does not generalize to the inserted 'be' ('what you'll be doing'), so UNKNOWN (undetected, since plain title-case with no family match is correctly rejected by this milestone's own regression-fix rule) is an accepted, honest outcome here, not a forced failure. Confirmed on first run: classifies as not-a-heading (UNKNOWN-equivalent, safe) -- exactly the anticipated, pre-declared uncertainty.
Fresh RESPONSIBILITY-family phrasing via the respons* root, distinct from the main corpus's 'Key Responsibilities'/'Position Responsibilities'.

A LEARNING-family idiom combining 'What You'll' (RESPONSIBILITY-adjacent phrasing) with 'Gain' (LEARNING root) -- tests that the LEARNING root fires correctly even when the sentence ALSO superficially resembles a RESPONSIBILITY idiom opener.

Plausible real-world LEARNING-adjacent heading with no root-word match (no 'learning opportunit*'/'you will learn' phrase, just the bare word 'Learning' as an adjective) -- correctly left UNKNOWN by this milestone's deliberately narrow root set; UNKNOWN is the safe, honest, accepted outcome, not a failure.

A FIFTH fictional company (distinct from the main corpus's Lumenbridge/Coriander Labs/Vertrix Systems/Northfield Analytics), confirming the 'about <proper noun>' structural rule generalizes to a company name never seen in selecting or implementing Strategy C.
Word-order variant of the main corpus's 'Perks and Benefits' -- confirms the NON_QUALIFICATION root match is order-independent.
Fresh NON_QUALIFICATION phrasing via the 'accommodation' root, modeled on the real Manulife EEO/accommodation paragraph but as its own heading, not literally in the main corpus.

Plausible real-world logistics heading (schedule/remote-work policy) with no root-word match at all -- correctly UNKNOWN; a design that confidently resolved this to NON_QUALIFICATION with no supporting root would be overreaching, not a strength.
Colon-terminated, hyphenated-plural variant of 'Must Have'/'Must-Have Skills', confirming the must[- ]have* root generalizes to this inflection.

A single bare technology name on its own line -- the EXACT shape class (single bare title-cased word, no colon/caps/markdown, no family root) whose misclassification as a phantom heading was this milestone's own implementation-discovered regression (`tests/test_job_parser_segmentation.py::test_newline_separated_requirements_without_bullets`). Must stay NOT a heading.
A two-word bare requirement-list value (no colon, no family root -- 'experience' alone is not a family root word), confirming the regression fix generalizes beyond single-word lines.

controls.text: Our qualifications process is designed to be fair and transparent for every applicant.
controls.rationale: Ordinary sentence (terminal period, multiple clauses) containing the REQUIRED-family root 'qualifications' -- must never be treated as a heading despite the root match, confirming the sentence-terminal-punctuation shape gate still takes priority over any root match.

controls.text: We are proud of our growth and the opportunities it creates for our employees.
controls.rationale: Ordinary marketing sentence containing both 'growth' and 'opportunities' (the LEARNING root's two key words) but NOT as the fixed 'growth opportunit*' phrase, and ending in a period -- must never be mistaken for a LEARNING heading.

All-caps rendering of an idiom already covered in the main corpus in title-case/lowercase/colon forms, but not previously tested in pure ALL-CAPS -- confirms the is_all_caps strong-signal branch and the PREFERRED root both fire together correctly.
A deeper Markdown heading level (4 '#' characters) than any main-corpus entry tested (which went up to '###'), confirming the markdown-leader strip is not hardcoded to a specific depth.
